disks.label: Current reinspection
disks.summary: 22 drives rechecked; two Shed drives remain unavailable.
evidence: All 22 freshly inspected drives report SMART overall pass / no NVMe critical warning. The two unreachable Shed disks are explicitly unknown.
The GPU boot NVMe is quiet in a fresh 55-second sample: 0.082 MiB/s reads, queue 0.013 and 1.10% busy. The Temporal/DCGM read storm is absent in this window.
Elite data NVMe remains 74% endurance used. Its boot NVMe estimate crossed 1%→2%; both unsafe-shutdown counters rose by one, without identifying cause.
Control-plane etcd fsync p99 remains 42.26 ms; its dedicated physical SSD averaged about 2.02 ms writes. Correlate tail latency with CPU steal before assigning a single cause.
NAS pools are ONLINE with no known data errors. AI-pool stripe exposure, single-disk Backup10T, warm BigTank drives and inherited sync=disabled remain architectural concerns.
disks.limitations: Physical identity matched on 21 Proxmox/NAS drives and Pi model/device; the VM and guest mount paths retain their baseline mapping timestamp. Passive I/O reflects current workload, not maximum performance.

resources.summary: VPA is making changes; fixed limits still require deliberate sizing.
evidence: 130 VPA policies observed. Prometheus estimates about 58 in-place pod updates, 58 applied admission adjustments and one eviction over 24 hours. These are counter-rate estimates, not exact event counts.
Five of six nodes are Ready. Shed readiness and pressure conditions are Unknown; missing usage is not zero load.
Grafana main container uses about 389 MiB under its deployed 2 GiB limit. DCGM uses about 526 MiB under 2 GiB; neither reclaimed pages in the 91-second sample.
Control-plane CPU steal is about 6.0%; SFF worker steal about 7.5%. This keeps hypervisor contention in the control-plane latency investigation.

Fresh physical MemAvailable: Threadripper 18.71 GiB, Dell 7.48 GiB, SFF 12.16 GiB, Elite 5.05 GiB, NAS 47.15 GiB and Pi 6.05 GiB. NAS ARC uses 315.60 GiB as cache with no recorded memory throttles; ARC allocation alone is not application pressure.
resources.label: Current reinspection
resources.limitations: Usage and VPA recommendations are current. Host DIMMs and any explicitly dated placement policy details remain baseline observations.

spread.summary: Most volumes still have only one configured Longhorn copy.
evidence: 81 Longhorn volumes observed: 79 configured with one copy and two with two copies, including retained volumes. All currently attached volumes report healthy.
Shed is unavailable; Intercept requires the RTL-SDR USB label found only on that host, so moving an ordinary pod cannot restore the missing hardware.
The tables below refresh current workload replicas, actual pod hosts, PVC replica counts and disk paths. A healthy single-copy volume has met its configuration, not gained redundancy.

thrashing.summary: Temporal, DCGM and Grafana repairs are still holding.
evidence: Temporal: latest completed 21:55 UTC run succeeded in four seconds with 1 GiB limit and 240-second deadline. The 22:00 capture caught the following Job just starting.
DCGM: running since 05:11 UTC with zero restarts; 4,030/4,030 successful scrapes. About 526 MiB in use; parent and container limits are both 2 GiB.
Grafana: running since 14:08 UTC with zero restarts. 941/942 scrapes succeeded; the single failed scrape preceded the new container start during rollout.
Both DCGM and Grafana added zero file refaults, direct reclaim, limit events or full memory stalls in a 91-second direct cgroup sample ending 21:59 UTC.
Fresh physical GPU boot SSD at 22:01–22:02 UTC: 0.082 MiB/s reads, queue 0.013 and 0.61 ms average reads; no severe queueing during this 55-second sample.
thrashing.label: Current reinspection
thrashing.limitations: A healthy sampled window and sustained pod uptime are strong repair evidence, not proof that all storage latency is solved.

health.summary: PostHog’s broker PVC is full; existing data and backup faults remain.
evidence: PostHog Redpanda’s 8 GiB PVC has zero available bytes and aborts with No space left on device. Ingestion-general and property-defs-rs fail behind it. The GPU host filesystem still has about 268 GB free: this is an application-volume boundary.
Intercept is Pending because its only RTL-SDR host, Shed, is unavailable. SurfSense Redis still has the same AOF corruption; Flatnotes still fails opening its Whoosh index.

Perplexica is the only failed latest snapshot among 35 policies. Last success was September 7 at 03:10 UTC, about 66.8 hours before this capture; the mover cannot read root-owned mode-0600 config.json.
The other 34 policies have successful latest snapshots. Kopia reports 1,412 index blobs above its 1,000 threshold despite recorded quick and full maintenance.
health.label: Current reinspection
health.limitations: No new isolated restore drill was performed. A successful backup can preserve an already-broken application state.

findings.title: PostHog: restore broker disk headroom
findings.evidence: 8 GiB Redpanda PVC is full; application ingestion is failing.
findings.action: Review the backing pool and expand the PVC through Git, then inspect effective retention and backlog. Do not delete queue data by default.
findings.verify: Broker becomes Ready, disk has sustainable free headroom, ingestion resumes and backlog drains.

findings.title: Shed / Intercept: restore the hardware path
findings.evidence: Shed node is Unknown and the only eligible RTL-SDR host.
findings.action: Establish whether shutdown was intentional; inspect power/link/host reachability or deliberately relocate the physical SDR.
findings.verify: Node and device are available; Intercept schedules and its real receiver path works.

findings.title: Control-plane storage: investigate continuing latency
findings.evidence: Current etcd fsync p99 42.26 ms and backend commit p99 60.52 ms.
findings.action: Correlate physical write latency with Proxmox CPU steal before selecting a disk migration.
findings.verify: Repeat a comparable window with improved etcd latency and no loss of control-plane responsiveness.

findings.title: Perplexica: repair backup ownership
findings.evidence: Latest backup PermissionDenied; last good snapshot approximately 66.8 hours old.
findings.action: Correct mover ownership using the documented root-owned-data exception; preserve application permissions.
findings.verify: A fresh scheduled snapshot succeeds and an isolated restore reads the expected data.

findings.title: Redis and Flatnotes: deliberate one-time data recovery
findings.evidence: Redis AOF corruption and Whoosh index EOF recur.
findings.action: Preserve originals, use the native repair/rebuild procedure, and keep recovery out of permanent startup scripts.
findings.verify: Redis loads its intended state; Flatnotes lists and searches preserved notes; application functions pass.

findings.title: Kopia: inspect index compaction
findings.evidence: 1,412 index blobs; maintenance runs are recorded.
findings.action: Review compaction/epoch behavior and maintenance history before changing intervals or taking over leases.
findings.verify: Index health improves while ordinary backups and a restore remain successful.

findings.title: Temporal / DCGM / Grafana: continue observation
findings.evidence: Correct limits deployed; latest runtime checks are healthy.
findings.action: Keep the merged budgets and monitor comparable workload/backup windows.
findings.verify: Scheduled recovery completes; exporter and Grafana stay healthy without renewed reclaim storms.
